name: Competitor update to campaign brief
summary: Check every page of your competitors and write a competitor update on what changed and why it matters. Once you approve (and edit) the update, turn it into a campaign brief for the response. Both wait for approval before they're saved to Google Docs.

inputs.label: Only these competitors
inputs.help: Comma-separated names from the Competitors page. Blank = all.

inputs.label: What campaigns are for
inputs.example: Pipeline from mid-market teams evaluating alternatives
inputs.help: Steers the brief's objective. Blank = the brief proposes one.

config.system: You are a competitive-intelligence analyst for a B2B software company. Be specific, short and factual; never invent numbers, features or dates that are not in the input.
config.prompt:
These competitor pages changed since the last check (lines starting with + were added, - removed):

{{outputs.watch.text}}

Write a competitor update for our marketing team. Plain text with these headings:
Headline: one sentence on the most important move.
What changed: one short paragraph per competitor, old versus new.
Why it matters to us: compared with our product facts and positioning.
Who it affects: which buyers or customer segments.
What we don't know yet: open questions the changes don't answer.
Skip changes that are only layout, dates or wording noise, and say so if that's all there is.

nodes.name: Turn the update into a campaign brief

config.system: You are a B2B product marketer who writes campaign briefs. Use only claims backed by our product facts; never attack the competitor by name in customer-facing messaging.
config.prompt:
Turn this approved competitor update into a campaign brief for our response.

Competitor update:
{{outputs.approve_update.content}}

What our campaigns are for (may be blank): {{input.campaign_goal}}

Plain text. Write each heading below exactly as named, on its own line, followed by its content; the text in brackets is guidance for you, not part of the heading:
Campaign name
Why now [the competitor move, in two sentences]
Objective [one measurable goal]
Target audience [who, and what they care about]
Key message [one sentence]
Proof points [three to five, each backed by our product facts]
Channels and deliverables [what to make for each channel]
Call to action
Timeline [a two-to-four-week plan]
Success metrics
Risks and claims to avoid
